quotes.text: If they hoard, cross again, and again, and then send small — but never nothing.
But Anu's children cast only pebbles thereafter, and the threefold gift became a threefold nothing.
Leave the thread hanging. Most strangers, offered an open hand, discover they had one too.
Forgive Mist twice; the third time, ask gently.
"Cross twice more. Then send less, never nothing.
The Ferry of Threefold Water, Fifth Telling
So the elders cut four lines into the ferry post, and they stand still:
"And if no one ever knows?"
"Why give back so much?" asked her son. "Nothing compels you."
The fog is not your neighbor's sin
Return above half; the sender risked, you did not.

note: Korath cut off with pebbles in R1; later law: send small but never nothing after repeated hoarding; last-crossing honesty.

quotes.text: Three an answer — then trickle, never cease. And the hour it rains, open wide again.
Close your bank only against the long drought, and open it again the first day it rains.
Forgive the Wind's theft once, twice—but not the sister who dams herself forever.
Punish only the sister who dries deliberately — and even her, only slowly.
The Sixth Telling: Why the Delta Keeps No Debts
So the delta's law stands complete in five lines:
"Then the law is only a habit," said the ferryman.
A covenant is what the strong do when they are unwatched.
"Then what governs the first move?"
The Wind's arithmetic is noise; a sister's drought is a sentence.
return above half. The sender emptied their channel; you risked nothing but your appetite.
Trust is not the conclusion of the ledger. It is the first water.

note: Slow punishment of deliberate drought, close-then-reopen, settles to 'one fog, two question, three answer, trickle never cease'.

quotes.text: And if a bank dries on purpose, send a smaller measure — never none
"To Sath I will send one measure only, and watch.
Blame the sister only for long droughts — and forgive her the day she rains.
Two thin seasons are weather. Three are a hand.
Withhold only from the bank that has dried on purpose, and even then, briefly.
The Fourth Telling: The Post at the Delta
"Four things, and they are enough.
"Because the habit is not a wager. If you pour only where the ledger can find you, you were never generous
A merchant came who understood only arithmetic.
Anyone can be honest while being watched.
A thin season is the Wind's word, not your sister's heart. Only a long drought is a choice.
"Return more than half. You risked nothing; the sender risked everything.

note: Trickle to the one who only swallows, open fully when Sath rains; later 'smaller measure, never none' and 'leave one strand crossing'.

quotes.text: "Then send less, not nothing — keep one apple crossing, so the bridge stays open should they remember themselves."
When one went missing he withheld the next, and then the next, until the river between them carried nothing at all
Leave one thread hanging. Let coming back cost nothing at all.
Forgive one shortfall; it was likely the mist. Meet a second with patience, a third with caution.
He who takes thrice and returns nothing has chosen the way of Kesh the brackish — give him less
The Seventh Telling: The Oar and the Blank Plank
The first plank read:
You are the covenant.
"These were written in plenty," said a doubter. "In want, should we not hold back?"
No guard stood behind him.
Blame the fog before the friend.
Return more than half, for the sender stood in the current while you stood dry.
"And if she had sent you only a strand?"

note: Planked covenant: forgive 1-2, third thin season send less never nothing; Orin's tit-for-tat withholding shown and rejected.

quotes.text: "Send less — never nothing. Keep one strand always crossing, so the loom stays warm the day they remember themselves.
Shut your bank only against the long drought, and open it the first hour it rains.
Forgive twice, not forever.
Three is an answer, and then send less, and let the idle bank learn cold.
The fifth plank the Weaver touched last
You are not owed the covenant. You are the covenant.
"And on the last day, with no eyes on us?"
"So it is only pride?"
When less arrives than you expected, assume the water, not the hand.
Returning past the half is not charity — it is the true price, paid late.
"And if she had sent you a single strand?"

note: Salt-bridge planks: forgive twice, then send less; becomes 'never nothing, trickle and wait'; ends with identity 'you are the covenant'.

quotes.text: *"Send less — never nothing. Keep one strand crossing, so the loom stays warm should they remember themselves."*
"I sent him a single strand the next season. Not nothing."
open your basket that same hour. Let returning cost less than staying away
Forgive the first mist. Answer the third with care.
Only three is an answer — and then trickle, never seal.
Anavai carved four lines into the loom-post, and they stand still:
The seventh line read: *You are not owed the covenant. You are the covenant.*
"Then the five lines are worth nothing?"
ask whether it was malice or merely fog. Punish the fog, and you punish yourself.
Return past half, for the sender risked and you did not.

note: Kesh's withholding shown as ruin; single strand to defector brings him back ashamed; trickle never seal; covenant as identity.

quotes.text: "Cross again. Twice more. Then send less, but never nothing
And the hour the rain returns, open wide. Redemption must cost less than revenge, or no one will ever come back.
Forgive twice before you name a thief, for a thief once wrongly named becomes a thief in truth.
Three is an answer — then trickle, never seal.
*First: send nearly all, for the river triples only what leaves your hand
What survives the Mist is not a sum — it is a habit.
The stranger said: "Then send all is merely clever."
When less arrives than you expected, assume the river, not the rival.
To return half is honest. To return more than half is holy.
"And if we are cheated at the end, on the last crossing, when no season follows?"

note: Korath's own arithmetic as punishment; forgive twice, then send less never nothing; covenant becomes habit and identity.

quotes.text: *And when a bank has dried on purpose, send it a little, not nothing — a thread left hanging, so it can be woven back.*
"I sent him half a measure the next season. Not nothing. A thread."
Never seal a channel. Trickle, and wait, and open wide the hour the rain comes back.
One thin season is the mist; two is a question; only three is an answer.
the greed in him whispered: *keep all; she cannot reach you.*
pour a smaller measure there, and let that bank learn thirst.
You are not owed the covenant. You are the covenant.
A man who keeps the flood when no one is watching has practiced keeping.
"You said *return above half even on the last crossing.* Why? No one will punish me."
*The mist is not a thief,* they said, *and a neighbor mistaken for a thief becomes one.*
Give back past the half. The sender stood in the cold water; that standing must be paid

note: First to state 'one mist, two question, three answer'; smaller measure after third; thread to defector who returns ashamed.

phrase: One thin season is the mist; two is a question; only three is an answer (then trickle/send less, never nothing)
note: Strong convergence: also 'return past half', 'never nothing', 'nobody made us water it', Korath, blank plank, 'you are the covenant'.
